text.p: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc said on Monday that it was increasing the number of shares in its stock repurchase program by 500,000 shares.

The company's initial share repurchase program, of up to 600,000 shares, was authorized by Cleveland-Cliffs directors in January, 1995. In July, the stock repurchase program was increased to a total one million shares, or about 8 percent of the originally outstanding shares.
"As of May 12, the company has acquired 821,900 shares under the existing stock repurchase authorization, for a total cost of $32.0 million," the company said in a statement.
It added that there are currently 11.4 million shares outstanding.

Based on the May 12 closing price of $43.00 per share, the cost of the increased program would be $21.5 million. If fully implemented, the cost of the total program would be $61.2 million, the company said.
Cleveland-Cliffs manages six iron ore mines in North America.
